samples.summary: Eagerly-loaded authenticated shell now statically imports the docs/board/slides/sheets engines, defeating App.tsx's lazy route splitting
samples.evidence: `App.tsx:8` imports `PrivateRoute` statically (every other route is `lazy(...)`, see App.tsx:15-32). `PrivateRoute.tsx:7` now imports `OfflineRuntime` statically, and `offline-runtime.tsx:11` statically imports `@/lib/offline-copy-recovery`, which at `offline-copy-recovery.ts:6,8,9,10` pulls in `@/app/documents/apply-imported-content`, `@/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store`, `@/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store` and `@/app/board/yorkie-board-store`. Those in turn are value-importers of the engine packages: `apply-imported-content.ts:3` (`initialSpreadsheetDocument` from `@wafflebase/sheets`), `:12` (`SYNTHETIC_SLIDE_ID` from `@wafflebase/board`), and `yorkie-board-store.ts:39-40` (`bandBlockNumerics` from `@wafflebase/docs`, `boardToSlidesDocument` from `@wafflebase/board`). The result is that a user who only opens the documents list downloads board/docs/slides/sheets engine code that `vite.config.ts` manualChunks (`sheet-core`, `slides-editor-engine`, `notes-editor-engine`) and the route-level `lazy()` calls exist to keep off that path. The fix belongs on the new code: `recoverOfflineCopy`/`describeArchivedDocument` should be reached through a dynamic `import()` inside the toast action rather than a top-level import.

samples.summary: OfflineRuntime runs for every signed-in user even though the pinned SDK makes the feature unreachable
samples.evidence: `PrivateRoute.tsx:35` renders `<OfflineRuntime userId={...} />` unconditionally, and `offline-runtime.tsx` gates on neither `supportsClientKey()` nor `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` — unlike every other surface, which the diff is explicit about gating (`settings/page.tsx:35`, `sync-status-chip.tsx` `offerOffline`, `use-durable-document.ts:128`). `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` to `0.7.22`, below `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (`yorkie-capabilities.ts`), so nothing can ever be persisted on this build. Consequence for every authenticated session today: an IndexedDB database (`wafflebase-offline`) is created, a 30-day sweep runs, and an extra `GET /documents` request is issued (`offline-runtime.tsx:4`, `fetchDocuments`) purely to reconcile a store that is guaranteed empty.

samples.summary: `vi.stubGlobal('__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__', ...)` cannot override an identifier Vite `define` substitutes at transform time
samples.evidence: `vite.config.ts` adds `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(...)` to the `define` block, which textually replaces the identifier in `yorkie-capabilities.ts` (`typeof __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ === "string" ? __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ : "0.0.0"`). Two suites nevertheless try to change it at runtime: the new `sync-status-chip.test.tsx` case "never promises to save the changes it is shown beside" does `vi.stubGlobal('__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__', '0.7.23')` and then asserts `options.action?.label` is truthy, and `yorkie-capabilities.test.ts` drives every case through `vi.stubGlobal`. If `define` is applied in the vitest transform (it is by default) the chip case fails, because `supportsClientKey()` returns the baked `0.7.22`; if it is not applied, `yorkie-capabilities.ts` always reads `"0.0.0"` outside a browser build and the production substitution path is never exercised. Either way one of the two suites is not testing what it names. The fix belongs on the new code — expose the version through an injectable/module-level read rather than a bare `define` identifier.

samples.summary: design-sandbox's `define` block mirrors the frontend's but was not given the new `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` constant
samples.evidence: `packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:180-190` states outright that its `define` block "Mirrors `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts`" because "Scene source IS real app source" and "an undefined global is a hard failure". It defines `process.env` and `__APP_VERSION__` but not `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, which `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts` now adds. Scenes mount real frontend components through `@/` (`packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/aliases.ts:66`, `providers.tsx:65` lazily loads `@/app/Layout`), so any scene that reaches `sync-status-chip.tsx` or `settings/page.tsx` evaluates `supportsClientKey()`. The `typeof` guard in `yorkie-capabilities.ts` keeps this from throwing, so the sandbox silently renders the feature as unavailable rather than crashing — hence minor rather than major.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` and `removeMember` now issue two extra network round-trips before the destructive call, on paths whose callers assume a single request
samples.evidence: `documentIdsIn` (`workspaces.ts:101-115`) calls `fetchWorkspace(ref)` and `fetchDocuments()` before the DELETE. Both `deleteWorkspace` and `removeMember` are driven from react-query mutations in `packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:133` and `:182`, which surface `isPending` on a button — those now include a full `GET /documents` (all documents across every workspace the user belongs to, per `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:180-195`) before anything destructive happens. `url.test.ts` had to be relaxed from an all-URLs assertion to a `some(...)` assertion (`url.test.ts:153-175`) precisely because of these companion requests, which is the signal that the request shape of these two endpoints changed for every existing caller.

verdict.reason: Every link in the claimed chain checks out in the repo. App.tsx:8 imports PrivateRoute statically while all routes around it (App.tsx:15-32, 61-86, including Layout at :69) are lazy(); PrivateRoute.tsx:7 statically imports OfflineRuntime and renders it unconditionally for authenticated users (PrivateRoute.tsx:35); offline-runtime.tsx:8-11 has a top-level value import of recoverOfflineCopy/describeArchivedDocument (used at :167 and :191, no dynamic import anywhere in the file); offline-copy-recovery.ts:6-9 value-imports applyImportedContent, YorkieDocStore, YorkieSlidesStore, YorkieBoardStore; apply-imported-content.ts:3 and :12 value-import initialSpreadsheetDocument from @wafflebase/sheets and SYNTHETIC_SLIDE_ID from @wafflebase/board; yorkie-board-store.ts:17-40 value-imports from @wafflebase/slides, @wafflebase/docs and @wafflebase/board. vite.config.ts:382-386 aliases those packages to their src barrels, and manualChunks at vite.config.ts:248-299 exists precisely to keep sheet-core/slides-editor-engine/notes-editor-engine off routes that do not need them; harness.config.json:65-75 encodes that download shape as a gated budget enforced by scripts/verify-frontend-chunks.mjs. No lazy boundary or guard intervenes — the other eager-shell path to apply-imported-content (Layout -> upload-queue) is behind a lazy() at App.tsx:69, so this is a genuinely new eager edge. This is a cross-module invariant violation visible only outside the diff, which is in-lane; I have no named ground to refute.

finding.summary: Board recovery feeds `applyImportedContent` read-back `Element`s where it expects mapper-minted `ElementInit`s, so every attached connector is silently dropped from the recovered copy
finding.evidence: New caller: `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts:96` returns `{ type: 'board', elements: store.read().slides[0]?.elements ?? [] } as ImportedContent`. The out-of-diff consumer `applyBoardElements` (`apply-imported-content.ts:96-141`) builds `realIds` only from the mapper's private `__id` handle (`line 116: if (__id) realIds.set(__id, realId)`) and then remaps every connector endpoint through it (`line 126-131`): `remapEndpoint` returns `null` for an `attached` endpoint whose id is not in the map, and the connector is counted in `droppedConnectors` and skipped. Elements read back out of `YorkieBoardStore.read()` carry a real `id` and no `__id`, so `realIds` is empty and **every** attached connector in a recovered board is discarded. `recoverOfflineCopy` (`offline-copy-recovery.ts:~205`) also ignores the returned `ImportApplyResult.droppedConnectors`, so the outcome is reported with `complete: rebuilt.complete` and the user is told the copy is whole. This is the archive — by this feature's own design the only remaining copy of that work. The fix belongs on the new caller (remap ids, or pass through a board-aware writer).

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. The finding claims `applyBoardElements` builds `realIds` only from the mapper's private `__id` (quoting a nonexistent `line 116: if (__id) realIds.set(__id, realId)`). In the actual file, the key is produced by `handleOf()` at apply-imported-content.ts:63-65, which returns `element.__id ?? element.id`, and it is used at :149 and :153 (`if (handle) realIds.set(handle, realId)`). Elements read back from the store do carry a real `id` — `YorkieBoardStore.readElement` (yorkie-board-store.ts:370-397) emits `el.id` on every element returned by `read()` (:313-331) — so for the offline-copy recovery caller (offline-copy-recovery.ts:96) `realIds` is populated by the elements' own ids, `remapEndpoint` (:91-98) resolves each attached endpoint, and no connector is dropped. Group members are likewise registered by `mapDescendants` (:75-84). Dedicated tests cover exactly this scenario and assert connectors survive: apply-imported-content-board.test.ts:184-223 (read-back ids) and :225-254 (group member). The secondary observation that `recoverOfflineCopy` (offline-copy-recovery.ts:211) discards the returned `ImportApplyResult` is factually true, but its stated impact depends on the false premise that every attached connector is dropped; with the handle fallback present it is not a data-loss bypass and does not block under the blast-radius rubric.
